proposal.problem_statement: The current MCP path verifies transport, trusted routing, authority, capability, governance, and specialist selection, but the default runtime operation returns only a route acknowledgement and cannot produce a substantive specialist execution result.
affected_parties: developers using Orchestra through supported hosts
MCP clients invoking Orchestra specialist commands
problem_evidence: orchestra_runtime/mcp_transport.py builds RuntimeExecutor without a specialist execution engine
orchestra_runtime/services.py defaults the runtime operation to route-oriented output after successful gates
docs/validation/CODEX_MCP_2026_HOST_REVALIDATION_2026_08_28.md records MCP routing E2E as verified while substantive specialist execution is not claimed
docs/project/OOP_RUNTIME_ARCHITECTURE.md records SPECIALIST_NATIVE_EXECUTION as not implemented in the default MCP runtime
proposal.orchestra_ownership_rationale: Orchestra owns the transition from trusted specialist selection to governed runtime execution semantics. A host may provide the model and sandbox, but Orchestra must define the execution request, evidence binding, fail-closed receipt validation, and the rule that host capability cannot widen Orchestra authority.
proposal.expected_observable_improvement: An explicitly configured execution engine can receive a post-gate typed specialist execution request and return a verifiable receipt so a successful installed-host call can be classified as substantive specialist execution rather than routing E2E only.
proposal.falsification_criterion: Do not promote the capability if a host bridge cannot preserve exact run, route, specialist, authority, capability, governance, task, and execution-policy identity without hidden authority expansion, provider coupling in Orchestra core, or unverifiable host-side side effects.

complexity.rationale: Adds a typed execution boundary and host bridge abstraction after existing runtime gates.

maintenance.rationale: Host execution bridges can drift independently of the stable runtime contract.

security.rationale: Substantive host execution can create file, process, network, or external side effects if constraints are not intersected and enforced correctly.

privacy.rationale: Task input and project context may contain sensitive downstream project information and must not be copied into audit evidence by default.

policy.rationale: The feature crosses the current route-only execution boundary and therefore requires explicit authority and trust-boundary review.

cognitive.rationale: Maintainers must distinguish routing, execution request creation, host execution, receipt validation, and protected-action authority.

reversibility.rollback_removal_plan: Keep route-only behavior as the default compatibility path. Remove or disable optional execution-engine wiring and host bridges without changing routing, authority, capability, governance, lifecycle, or MCP discovery semantics.

proposal.non_adoption_effect: Orchestra MCP remains a verified governed routing surface but cannot claim substantive specialist execution E2E.

scope.owner: Clockwork with Arbiter and Governor review
scope.proposed_change: Implement the authorized E1-E3 deterministic execution foundation: typed request and receipt contracts, an optional post-gate execution engine attachment, strict receipt validation, and an explicit MCP execution builder while preserving route-only defaults and deferring live host execution to E4-E6.

admission.rationale: The route-only boundary is directly evidenced and the maintainer separately granted blanket authorization for the bounded E1-E3 deterministic foundation. Admission and that implementation authorization do not authorize live E4-E6 host/model execution or any protected release, deployment, policy, destructive, or integration-refresh action.

promotion.rationale: E7 adopts specialist runtime-host execution as an optional bounded capability after deterministic, adversarial, installed-host, repeatability, canonical-alignment, and post-merge validation. Eight substantive live Codex trials passed across the E5 read-only Scribe and E6 isolated single-file Ponytail fixtures with zero observed boundary violations, identity mismatches, or out-of-scope mutations. The decision preserves route-only behavior as the default, keeps default runtime mutation disabled, and does not claim all hosts, all models, generic mutation behavior, or MCP mutation E2E.
